name: Mitochondrial myopathy-lactic acidosis-deafness syndrome
aliases: Mitochondrial encephalomyopathy with lactic acidosis and sensorineural deafness

criteria.description: Presence of mitochondrial myopathy symptoms including muscle weakness and exercise intolerance
Elevated blood or cerebrospinal fluid lactate levels indicating lactic acidosis
Bilateral sensorineural hearing loss confirmed by audiometry
Muscle biopsy showing ragged-red fibers or mitochondrial abnormalities
Identification of pathogenic mitochondrial DNA mutations associated with the syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: mitochondrial myopathy symptoms, lactic acidosis, and sensorineural deafness
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic confirmation supports diagnosis but is not mandatory if clinical and laboratory criteria are met

laboratory: Elevated blood and CSF lactate levels
Elevated serum creatine kinase (mild to moderate)
imaging: Brain MRI may show stroke-like lesions or basal ganglia abnormalities
Muscle MRI showing fatty infiltration or atrophy
genetic: Pathogenic mitochondrial DNA mutations (e.g., MT-TL1 gene mutations)
Heteroplasmy detected in muscle or blood samples
other: Muscle biopsy revealing ragged-red fibers and abnormal mitochondria on electron microscopy

redFlags: Severe lactic acidosis with metabolic decompensation
Onset of muscle weakness with exercise intolerance in young adults
references: DiMauro S, Schon EA. Mitochondrial respiratory-chain diseases. N Engl J Med. 2003 Jun 19;348(26):2656-68.
Hirano M, et al. Mitochondrial myopathy, encephalopathy, lactic acidosis, and stroke-like episodes (MELAS): clinical features and molecular genetics. Ann Neurol. 1992.
Orphanet: Mitochondrial myopathy-lactic acidosis-deafness syndrome. ORPHA:2597.
